newsitem.title: USA: Anheuser-Busch ends talks with Czech brewer.
newsitem.headline: Anheuser-Busch ends talks with Czech brewer.

text.p: Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc said on Monday it had ended negotiations with Czech brewer Budejovicky Budvar and the government of the Czech Republic regarding a Budweiser trademark agreement.

"Due to our success in selling our Budweiser beer in disputed markets in Europe under the Bud brand name, coupled with a number of recent litigation successes with both the Budweiser and Bud names, it is no longer necessary for us to have a trademark settlement to develop our Budweiser business in Europe," Chairman Jack Purnell said in a statement.

Anheuser-Busch said it sells its beer under the Budweiser name in 11 European countries and under the Bud name in nine other European countries. Both brands have virtually identical labels except for the name, it added.
It said the Budvar brewery, established in 1895, started using Budweiser on its label in the 1960s.
Anheuser said that since its dispute with Budvar has been limited primarily to certain countries in Europe and North Africa, it has not had a significant impact on its international growth.

The company said it has been successful in establishing its trademark rights in many new European markets through litigation. It has obtained favorable rulings in trademark disputes with Budvar in the United Kingdom, Spain, France, Portugal, Sweden, Norway, Finland and elsewhere.
"We are prepared to appeal any unfavorable decisions and, if necessary, modify our commercial activities with alternate brand names," Purnell said.
He said Anheuser-Busch dropped its efforts for an equity partnership with Budvar two years ago, "and today we have ended all efforts for a trademark settlement."
